intended_object: A property P of ring homomorphisms between commutative rings has this property when it is "local" in the following sense: if f : R → S is a ring map and r₁,…,rₙ are finitely many elements generating the unit ideal of R, and P holds for each induced map R_{rᵢ} → S_{f(rᵢ)}, then P holds for f. Taken from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The body quantifies over all commutative rings R and S in universe u, over every ring hom f : R →+* S and every Finset s ⊆ R with Ideal.span s = ⊤. It requires that P (Localization.awayMap f r) for all r ∈ s implies P f. Here `Localization.awayMap f r : Localization.Away r →+* Localization.Away (f r)` is exactly the induced map R_r → S_{f(r)}. This is the standard "local on the base" condition for properties of ring maps (as in the Stacks Project, restricted to finite covers). The restriction to finite sets is intended: this is what separates it from `RingHom.OfLocalizationSpan`, and the docstring notes that the two are equivalent via `RingHom.ofLocalizationSpan_iff_finite`. Fixing one universe for R and S is the usual Mathlib convention for these meta-properties, not a loss of generality that matters. The definition is at its natural generality (any commutative rings), so it is faithful.
